name: Rosewood Inn of the Anasazi
insider_take: A sophisticated pueblo-style sanctuary where ancient Anasazi craftsmanship meets modern luxury in the heart of Santa Fe's historic plaza.
whats_special: This intimate 58-room hotel occupies a prime location just steps from Santa Fe Plaza, featuring authentic adobe architecture with hand-carved vigas, kiva fireplaces, and original Native American artwork throughout. The property sits on land once inhabited by the Anasazi people over 1,000 years ago, creating a profound connection to the area's ancient heritage.
pro_tip: Book a room on the upper floors for stunning views of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains, and time your visit during late September to catch the spectacular fall aspen colors that paint the mountainsides gold.
dont_miss: The hotel's renowned Anasazi Restaurant serves innovative Southwestern cuisine using indigenous ingredients, while the nearby Palace of the Governors (America's oldest continuously occupied public building since 1610) hosts Native American artisans selling authentic jewelry and pottery under its historic portal daily.
pros: Prime location steps from Santa Fe Plaza and historic attractions
Authentic Southwestern architecture with Native American-inspired design
Intimate boutique property with personalized luxury service
Award-winning Anasazi Restaurant featuring regional cuisine
cons: Limited on-site amenities due to boutique size
